Foreign function interface

Source: R/ffi.R
ffi_register_target.Rd

Ports of jax.ffi.register_ffi_target, jax.ffi.register_ffi_type, jax.ffi.register_ffi_type_id, jax.ffi.register_ffi_target_as_batch_partitionable and jax.ffi.include_dir.

Usage

ffi_register_target(name, fn, platform = "cpu", api_version = 1L, ...)

ffi_register_type(name, type_registration, platform = "cpu")

ffi_register_type_id(name, obj, platform = "cpu")

ffi_register_target_as_batch_partitionable(name)

ffi_include_dir()

Arguments

name

The name of the target (or of the type).

fn

The handler: the address of the symbol defined with XLA_FFI_DEFINE_HANDLER_SYMBOL, as an external pointer or the result of getNativeSymbolInfo(); or a named list with element execute holding it (the other FFI stages, instantiate, prepare and initialize, cannot be registered through the PJRT plugin interface jaxR uses).

platform

The target platform: "cpu" (the default), "cuda", "rocm", or the platform name XLA uses.

api_version

The custom call API of the handler: 1 (the default) for the typed FFI. Handlers of the earlier custom call API (0) cannot be registered through the PJRT plugin interface.

...

Not used (JAX passes extra arguments to xla_client.register_custom_call_target).

type_registration

For ffi_register_type(): a list with element type_id, the address of the XLA_FFI_TypeId of the type (filled in by XLA when it holds 0), and optionally type_info, the address of its XLA_FFI_TypeInfo.

obj

Not used.

Value

ffi_register_target(), ffi_register_type() and ffi_register_target_as_batch_partitionable() return NULL invisibly; ffi_include_dir() returns the directory of the XLA FFI headers.

Details

A foreign function is a typed XLA FFI handler written in C or C++ with the headers in ffi_include_dir() (#include "xla/ffi/api/ffi.h", then XLA_FFI_DEFINE_HANDLER_SYMBOL), compiled into a shared library and loaded with dyn.load(). ffi_register_target() registers it under a name; ffi_call() calls it.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dir <- tempfile("ffi")
dir.create(dir)
writeLines(c(
  '#include "xla/ffi/api/ffi.h"',
  'namespace ffi = xla::ffi;',
  'static ffi::Error AddOne(ffi::Buffer<ffi::F32> x, float y,',
  '                         ffi::ResultBuffer<ffi::F32> out) {',
  '  for (size_t i = 0; i < x.element_count(); ++i)',
  '    out->typed_data()[i] = x.typed_data()[i] + y;',
  '  return ffi::Error::Success();',
  '}',
  'XLA_FFI_DEFINE_HANDLER_SYMBOL(add_one, AddOne,',
  '  ffi::Ffi::Bind().Arg<ffi::Buffer<ffi::F32>>().Attr<float>("y")',
  '    .Ret<ffi::Buffer<ffi::F32>>());'), file.path(dir, "add_one.cc"))
writeLines(c("CXX_STD = CXX17", paste0("PKG_CPPFLAGS = -I", ffi_include_dir())),
           file.path(dir, "Makevars"))
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "R"), c("CMD", "SHLIB", file.path(dir, "add_one.cc")),
        env = paste0("R_MAKEVARS_USER=", file.path(dir, "Makevars")))
dll <- dyn.load(file.path(dir, paste0("add_one", .Platform$dynlib.ext)))
ffi_register_target("add_one", getNativeSymbolInfo("add_one", dll))
x <- jnp_arange(4, dtype = "float32")
ffi_call("add_one", ShapeDtypeStruct(4L, "float32"))(x, y = as_jax(1, "float32"))
} # }
